questions.q: Which three courses make up the Job Ready stage of the SQL Server Database Administrator career path, in order?
options: T-SQL Development, T-SQL for Database Administrators, SQL Server Database Administration
SQL Server Database Administration, SQL Server Performance Tuning, Azure Database Administrator
T-SQL Development, SQL Server Performance Tuning, PowerShell Automation and DevOps for DBAs
SQL Server HA/Backup and Disaster Recovery, Azure Database Administrator, T-SQL Development
questions.explain: The Job Ready stage is T-SQL Development, then T-SQL for Database Administrators, then this course — SQL Server Database Administration — completing it in that order.

questions.q: What does completing this course and its capstone actually demonstrate, per the lesson's framing?
options: The ability to handle the combined situation a junior or full DBA role presents — an under-maintained server, a security gap, a production incident, and a schema change that must ship safely — not just isolated topic knowledge
Mastery of Azure-specific database administration
That the student has memorized every DMV name in SQL Server
That the student is ready for the Multi-Platform Databases stage without needing Advanced SQL Server first
questions.explain: The capstone deliberately combines the course's topics into one continuous, realistic scenario, which is closer to what an actual DBA role demands than isolated lessons alone.

questions.q: Which course opens the Advanced SQL Server stage that follows this one, and why does it make sense as the next step?
options: SQL Server Performance Tuning — because it builds on a server that's already healthy, secure, and maintained, going deeper into execution plans, indexing, and wait statistics
Azure Database Administrator — because cloud administration should come immediately after any on-prem course
NoSQL Document and Graph Databases — because it broadens platform exposure right away
PowerShell Automation and DevOps for DBAs — because automation is always the first advanced topic
questions.explain: The Advanced SQL Server stage opens with SQL Server Performance Tuning, which assumes the server is already stable, secure, and maintained (what this course covers) and focuses on making it fast.

questions.q: What is a 'portfolio artifact' in the sense this lesson uses the term?
options: A concrete, specific piece of real or realistic work — like the MERSQL01 capstone — written up to demonstrate actual skill to an employer, distinct from just a training exercise
A SQL Server backup file kept for disaster recovery purposes
A certificate of completion issued automatically at the end of a course
A collection of every quiz score earned throughout the course
questions.explain: The lesson recommends writing up the capstone's five-beat story with its specific numbers as a resume/portfolio piece — a demonstrable, defensible example of real skill, not just a course deliverable.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what makes the capstone's specific numbers (15-minute RPO, 12-minute incident resolution, a reversible schema deployment) valuable in a job interview?
options: They are concrete and defensible in detail, because the student actually performed the diagnostic and remediation work that produced them
They are impressive purely because they are numbers, regardless of whether the student understands how they were achieved
They eliminate the need to explain any of the underlying methodology
They only matter for DBA roles specifically at trucking or logistics companies
questions.explain: The value isn't the numbers alone — it's that the student can explain the mechanism behind each one because they did the actual diagnostic and remediation work across Lessons 64-68.
